piece.title: String Quartet in C major, Hob.III:77, Op.76 No.3 (“Emperor”)
piece.movement: II. Poco adagio; cantabile — Var. II
piece.why: Variation II: the hymn moves to the cello while Violin I plays a busy countermelody above it. Both planners mislabel the violin as the tune here; the cello's hymn is still kept.

plan.summary: This is still a sax trio built on the same idea. The alto carries the Violin 1 tune, the tenor plays the cello's walking line as a countermelody in the middle, and the baritone takes the lowest line, which is the viola's D/G pedal. The tune now stays at written pitch so it sits on top of the texture. To keep the real lowest line at the bottom, the Violin 2 inner part is the one we leave out.

assignments.reason: The main tune, played at pitch so it stays above the tenor and baritone. A few peak notes (A5, B5, D6) go above the alto's range, and only those will be dropped an octave. [checker moved this line -1 octave(s) to fit the range]
The tune continues. From here it sits entirely within the alto's range (F#4–G5), so nothing moves.
The cello's walking countermelody, including the scale run in m.56. It fits the tenor's warm middle register (F#3–G4) at pitch. [checker: mm. 40-59 at +0 octave(s) to fit the range]
The cello's walking countermelody, including the scale run in m.56. It fits the tenor's warm middle register (F#3–G4) at pitch. [checker: mm. 60-60 at +1 octave(s) to fit the range]
The viola's D/G pedal is the lowest line in this passage, so the baritone holds it at pitch (C3–C4) to anchor the trio. The long notes are easy and leave room to breathe.

dropped.reason: With only three players, Violin 2's inner line is the one we lose. The tune, the cello countermelody and the pedal bass already outline the harmony.
